name: Epsilon Indi B

input.source: Gaia DR3 6412596012146801152 catalogue position at J2016.0 (the brief gives no coordinate)

proper_motion_source: Gaia DR3 source 6412596012146801152: pmra*cosdec=3981.977 mas/yr, pmdec=-2466.832 mas/yr, ref epoch J2016.0 (TCB); parallax 270.658 mas applied (geocentric observer; SPHEREx LEO offset ignored)

grid.array_storage: PNG and .f32 rows are stored top-down (row 0 = north edge). FITS pixel y = NAXIS2-1-png_y; x is the same.

comparison_star.selection: Gaia DR3, 10<=G<=16.5, total PM<10 mas/yr, >=7 px from target, >=6 px from grid edge, no Gaia neighbour with G<G+2.5 within 20 arcsec; brightest passing

masked_core_area_px_within_6px.note: Count of co-add mask pixels (saturated or flagged in >=50% of frames, or no data) within 6 grid px of the predicted target position. For saturated stars this grows with brightness, so it is a qualitative brightness proxy, NOT a flux.

psf_wing_ratio_first_last_full.note: Sum of co-add surface brightness (MJy/sr, local-median-subtracted) in a 4-10 px annulus around the target, pixels unmasked in both visits. Band-averaged (each visit's co-add mixes the LVF wavelengths it sampled), assumes an unchanged PSF and includes any neighbours in the annulus: a variability indicator for saturated stars, not calibrated photometry.

notes: Frames: 452 used of 458 fetched; rejected {'wl_out_of_band': 6, 'offdetector': 0}. 2 frames had the target within 10.0 px of the strip/detector edge, so no forced photometry for them.

Input coordinate (Gaia DR3 6412596012146801152 catalogue position at J2016.0 (the brief gives no coordinate)) is 46.7 arcsec (7.6 px) from the mean-epoch (2026-01-01) proper-motion-corrected position the grid is centred on.

Epsilon Indi B is the unresolved Ba+Bb T-dwarf binary (about 0.7 arcsec apart), so the photometry is the combined light. Gaia DR3 6412596012146801152 (RUWE 4.3, consistent with binarity) was used for astrometry.

Blending with Eps Indi A: A (Gaia DR3 6412595290592307840, G=4.3) is 402.6 arcsec (65 grid px) west of B at the mean epoch, outside the 49x49 px (301 arcsec) grid and far outside the 2.5 px aperture, so there is no blend in the aperture. Its scattered-light halo does produce a background gradient toward the west (right) edge of the grid; the 6-10 px local-annulus background removes it at B's position.
Visits v1 (Apr-Jun 2025, D1/D4 only 3-4 frames) and v4 (Sep-Oct 2026, no D1/D4) are not full by the >=5-frames-in-every-band rule but are rich in D2/D3/D5/D6.
Brief: the challenge gives no coordinate for this target. input.* is the Gaia DR3 catalogue position at J2016.0.

Pixel data: SPHEREx Level-2 spectral images (spherex_dr1, plus spherex_qr3 where SIA returned them), read by HTTP range requests from s3://nasa-irsa-spherex (IMAGE and VARIANCE strips, row-tiled RICE FLAGS decompressed locally, WCS-WAVE table, EPSF row). One frame was checked byte-identical to the IRSA cutout service for IMAGE, FLAGS and VARIANCE.

Frame filter: the wavelength at the target pixel comes from the 'W' WCS (WAVE-TAB, sip=None) and must lie inside the detector's em_min..em_max. Visits are clusters with no gap >20 days. A visit is 'full' when every band D1-D6 has >=5 frames.

Co-adds: each frame has its sigma-clipped median subtracted (local zodi/background removal) and pixels with any of SUR_ERROR, TRANSIENT, OVERFLOW, NONLINEAR, NONFUNC, DICHROIC, MISSING_DATA, HOT, COLD, PHANMISS, PERSIST, OUTLIER, CROSSTALK, GHOST, GHOST_FPA, GHOST_EXT, STREAK, BLOOM, SNOWBALL or HALO masked. Frames are bilinearly resampled (normalised by the good-pixel weight, needing weight >=0.5) through the full SIP WCS onto the common grid, then median-combined per visit per band.
